#3898. Nvidia shareholders have filed a lawsuit against the tech company over claims that they were misled regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair

If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly quickly.

As it currently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

So I've been utterly consumed by WoW: Forever, which is a relief, because it's my job to write about it—and I've been powering ahead to 40, where a deeply oldschool grind to get my first mount awaits me. Before that, though, I had an absolutely lovely time futzing around The Riverglades, one of WoW: Forever's properly bespoke zones. As in, this thing wasn't in vanilla. This was cooked up and released in November.

Having quested through most of it in a blissful fugue state with some friends, we each came to the conclusion that it all feels very 2007, rather than 2006.

The Riverglades, which you can head to at about level 38, is saturated with quests. Even more so than the revamped and revisited zones from vanilla World of Warcraft. And while it absolutely has the classic zone's sense of scale, and none of these quests have the retail aura of on-rails cutscenes about them, I wasn't actually tasting vanilla.

One of the hallmarks of older, classic-style quest design is a bunch of disparate quests that have you scattering out towards the map—Riverglades, then, feels a lot more modern, in that it uses that scattershot point-of-interest guide as a baseline, then cleverly tucks away even more quests at your destination.

In one case, fighting through a ruined village flooded with Twilight's Blade, me and my compatriot saw a quest marker underground. It took ages for us to find a basement, which then yawned out into an open cavern with shadow-infused ogres and a cunning woman trapped in a cage with her own quest chain.

At which point it clicked: Oh, I'm playing The Burning Crusade again. The template was classic, sure, but the density and the branching paths and the clever redirects—that's all Outland, baby. There's even a set of swampy flats in the middle of The Riverglades pock-marked by orcish poachers that made me say, out loud: Oh, I'm in Nagrand again. Just without the floating islands.

And you know what, having had this unexpectedly adjacent nostalgic experience, I didn't hate it.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I do hope that Forever manages to preserve its more Vanilla aspects; I've written on this site quite recently about how I've adored just going on an adventure. Heck, I had the terrible idea to do the Scarlet Monastery as Alliance recently, and the quest chain leading up to the sword I wanted forced me to run all the way across Desolace to fight level 40 skeletons. It was great.

But The Burning Crusade, in many senses, was the best of both worlds. WoW hadn't been claimed by its Cataclysm-era propensity for goofs and pop culture references over atmosphere yet, but it also hadn't stuck doggedly to its vanilla quest design that was sometimes just flat-out bad.

In fact, many of Forever's new quests, even in other zones, have been built around plugging up awkward questing gaps, or giving players more to do in zones that've been otherwise barren. Which, as it turns out, just produces Outland 2.0. If the other levelling zones Blizzard adds to Forever are as Nagrand-flavoured as the Riverglades, I really don't mind at all.

#3896. Commandos: Origins Deluxe Edition coming to Switch 2 on December 15

Publisher Kalypso Media and developer Engine Software will release stealth tactics game Commandos: Origins Deluxe Edition for Switch 2 on December 15 for $59.99, the companies announced.

Commandos: Origins first launched for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam, Epic Games Store, and Microsoft Store on April 9, 2025, followed by PlayStation 4 and Xbox One on September 17, 2025.

Here is an overview of the Switch 2 version, via Kalypso Media:

Following its successful launch on other platforms in 2025, the legendary tactical stealth series is ready to take its next mission on the move—with both post-launch expansions, Shadows over Crete and No Man Left Behind, available to be purchased separately.

The Commandos: Origins Deluxe Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 takes players back to the very beginning of the elite special forces unit, telling the story of how the legendary Commandos came together. Led by Jack O’Hara, the Green Beret, players will infiltrate enemy territory, sabotage key targets and lead their elite squad in World War II.

On Nintendo Switch 2, players can put the Joy-Con 2 mouse controls to work for a more precise approach to battlefield command. Switch to mouse control to navigate the battlefield with greater accuracy, select targets and units with precision, and issue commands with the control expected from a tactical stealth classic. Furthermore GameChat and two-player cooperative multiplayer mode are supported, either online or via local split-screen.

The Commandos: Origins Deluxe Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 delivers the full experience by including the complete base game, six iconic Commando skins from Commandos 2 adapted for Commandos: Origins, a 3D printing template for the Green Beret, a digital Commandos: Origins calendar and the original soundtrack with 15 symphonic tracks.

Alongside the main campaign, both post-launch downloadable contents “Shadows over Crete” and “No Man Left Behind” on Nintendo Switch are available from day one, adding further missions and challenges to the Commandos’ World War II campaign. Each downloadable content is available for $14.99 USD.

The Commandos: Origins Deluxe Edition will be released digitally for Nintendo Switch 2 on December 15, 2026, for $59.99 USD

#3895. Marathon is becoming a whole new game next month with a roguelite PvE mode, a beta for a very Halo-esque team deathmatch mode, a vibey social space and more

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their plans for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

The previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the new runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few new weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

#3894. Mass Effect-like RPG The Expanse: Osiris Reborn ropes in David Gaider, the original lead writer of Bioware's Dragon Age series

"Focusing on certain aspects of the game's narrative."

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn looks like it's carrying the best bits of Mass Effect forward, and in an encouraging move, the developers have been collaborating with David Gaider.

Of course, David Gaider is best known as the lead writer on Dragon Age: Origins, Dragon Age 2 and Dragon Age: Inquisition - he's also often credited as the architect of its dark fantasy world Thedas. Gaider's post-BioWare career saw him open his own game development house Summerfall Studios, which most recently released an ambitious roleplaying musical called Stray Gods.

But he's now lending a hand to a game that's not too dissimilar to BioWare's other hugely famous roleplaying series, while still working on his own games at Summerfall.

"Alongside my work at Summerfall, I've also been collaborating with the Owlcat Games team on The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, focusing on certain aspects of the game's narrative. The Expanse has long been one of my favourite series, and so obviously I jumped at the opportunity to be involved," he wrote on BlueSky.

"The Owlcat team has been so great, it's really such a treat. One thing I enjoy is how responsive they are to the fans," Gaider added, pointing to how the studio recently recast the male version of its protagonist in response to feedback. The game's reworked and re-designed Martian Captain is now voiced by Blythe Melin.

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn shouldn't be confused for the other very Mass Effect-y RPG coming out next year, Exodus. Though it's good to hear that both upcoming projects have some BioWare veterans on board, especially after the famed developer was shut down and had its own promising, actual Mass Effect game cancelled.

Bertie enjoyed what he played of the upcoming game in Eurogamer's The Expanse preview, but also had some concerns about the developer's use of generative AI.

A Link Between Worlds is on Switch Online, apparently... or at least, Nintendo seems to think so

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

An official The Legend of Zelda website has listed the 3DS title A Link Between Worlds as available on Nintendo Switch Online, leading to speculation that the handheld's library could be coming to the service.

The Legend of Zelda fans are in a pretty good place when it comes to the series on Switch. If you have a Switch 2, you have access to every mainline entry in the series barring Four Swords Adventures, Twilight Princess, Phantom Hourglass, Spirit Tracks, A Link Between Worlds, and the somehow considered mainline Tri Force Heroes. And while Four Swords Adventures and Twilight Princess are on the cards thanks to the GameCube Nintendo Switch Online app, the handheld titles are generally seen as unlikely due to their dual screens.

However, on the Zelda Game History page on the Nintendo website, some have noticed an interesting disclaimer. You can click on each game to see a blurb about it, and with the games that are available to play on Nintendo Switch Online, there's a little mark showing this. Naturally this is present on the original NES game, Ocarina of Time, Wind Waker and the like, however, it's also present on The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds for the 3DS.

Obviously, there currently isn't a 3DS app available on Switch or Switch 2, and in theory, next in line would be the Wii, DS, and 3DS before we reach the Wii U – which already has all of its major titles on Switch – and then the Switch era itself. Theoretically, A Link Between Worlds would be easier to make work than the DS duology due to the second screen effectively being a menu screen.

However, I'm not sure I'd get my hopes up. Firstly, if the Game Boy Advance is exclusive to Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack users, there's no way that the 3DS would be on the regular Nintendo Switch Online subscription. And as a user on Reddit points out, The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages – which is already on Switch Online and specifically as part of the non-Expansion Pack subscription – is missing its "Playable with Nintendo Switch Online" label, so it's likely somehow been mixed up with A Link Between Worlds.

That being said, it does hammer home that Nintendo is currently letting one of the best Legend of Zelda games of all-time remain unplayable on modern hardware since the 3DS store was discontinued, so a 3DS Nintendo Switch Online would be appreciated, as many of the other comments on Reddit prove.

#3892. Ahead of GTA 6 and as concerns over genAI PC ports grow, Take-Two's CEO says they're revving up their "technical defences" and "legal activites" over piracy

"[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that"

It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are currently technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business issues they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended."

Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

#3891. Updated Xbox PC app promises 60% faster loading and easier access to games, but CEO Asha Sharma says there's "plenty more to do"

The Xbox PC app hasn't had the best track record in recent years, but Microsoft is promising that it's now much faster and easier to use than before.

Starting today, anyone part of the Xbox Insiders program can try out the new improvements. According to Microsoft, the updated Xbox PC app now boots up 60% faster, several pages can launch up to 50% faster, and in-app windows can open up to 65% faster. The company acknowledged that performance can vary based on your set up, internet connection, device, and so on.

The rest of the update involves "simpler navigation, updated filters, and new ways to organise your games," according to Xbox Wire, while social features are now included in the main navigation menu so you can start playing or chatting with friends quicker.

A faster Xbox PC app is certainly nice for players who regularly use it, though it's still missing a lot of the features that make Steam the go-to place to buy PC games. CEO Asha Sharma called the update "a meaningful improvement," but acknowledged there's still "plenty more to do."

Microsoft also said "it's easier to find what you're looking for" using the app's search function, and refreshed game cards and animations should give the platform "a cleaner look and feel."

Elsewhere, the revamped cloud gaming setup will roll out to even more people using web browsers, and more Xbox Insiders should hear about the program over the next few weeks. "The updated experience also makes it easier to find and play your games," the company said while bringing attention to its new light and dark modes. Supported smart TVs and VR headsets will get the updated cloud experience, as well.

Earlier this year, the console maker brought a selection of 'classic' games to PC for the first time ever - Blinx: The Time Sweeper, Conker: Live and Reloaded, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge and Fuzion Frenzy led the first batch. Mythic Achievements - the Platinum Trophy equivalent - went live for all Xbox players, too.

The MMA fighter and failed Irish presidential candidate had a small role in the 2016 shooter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Call of Duty doesn't have much luck with its stunt casting. Two years after Infinity Ward put Kevin Spacey in Advanced Warfare—before he was accused of sexual assault—it turned MMA fighter Conor McGregor into a future soldier, Captain Bradley Fillion, in Infinite Warfare.

McGregor's role was quite small, despite being one of the game's antagonists, and ended in his character's demise, but co-directors Jordan Hirsh and Taylor Kurosaki didn't want to cut any corners when it came to the mo-cap.

I got to work with Conor McGregor, and the story about Conor McGregor… We shot that in either 2015 or early 2016, but this is the height of him as a UFC fighter. And so of course I wanted him to do something really physical, to demonstrate how capable he is. He's shorter than me, but I was trying to explain to him the choreography that I wanted him to do at the beginning there, where he smashes the guy, and he grabbed me and flipped me onto the ground—very gently. And then did this punch [right in front of my face] that I could feel the wind from.

At the time, co-directors Hirsh and Kurosaki were trying to shake things up in regards to mo-cap. "I think that the folks at Infinity Ward probably thought I was a little crazy when I came in," Kurosaki tells us. "I think for every game they had done before that, you would maybe do some mocap or a cool takedown or a finisher, and then you'd have actors that would come into a VO booth and you'd have them come in one at a time and they'd read their lines and it’d be stitched together and then you're done. And they built a performance capture stage specifically for this project."

With Infinite Warfare, the team was doing full performance capture, so it needed its actors to get more physical.

Kurosaki remembers, after McGregor flipped him, that he "did this punch [right in front of my face] that I could feel the wind from. We're just rehearsing and figuring out the blocking. Everyone on the stage was, ‘Whoa, that was crazy! It was so fast!’ And of course, I had a different perspective than everyone else. Then everyone was laughing, and he helped me up, and I'm laughing. And then all of a sudden, this giant bead of sweat starts running down my face. I had this adrenaline, even though I knew I was perfectly safe. My body was just doing something that I couldn't control."

A few years later, McGregor started racking up criminal charges for assault. In 2019, he attacked a man for not accepting a drink in a Dublin pub. He pleaded guilty. In the same year, police in Ireland started investigating McGregor over allegations of multiple sexual assaults. He was not prosecuted, but a civil claim was made against him by Nikita Hand. In 2024, an Irish jury found that McGregor raped Hand.

Also in 2024, McGregor starred in Hitman, as one of its celebrity Elusive Targets—his second videogame role outside of the UFC games. IO Interactive stopped working with him after the ruling and removed him from the game as an Elusive Target.

Activision, unlike IO, left McGregor in the Infinite Warfare campaign. The fighter has not made any other videogame appearances since then. Prior to the ruling, he was a playable fighter in EA's UFC games, starting in 2014. He was the co-cover athlete in 2016's UFC 2 and the solo cover athlete in 2018's UFC 3. His last appearance in the series was in UFC 5 in 2023.

McGregor has had no scripted television cameos since 2024, appearing strictly as himself for promotional spots and interviews—including a guest appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in June 2026. Fallon and NBC were heavily criticised for inviting McGregor onto the show. He is also attached to host and executive-produce a Fox Nation competition series titled World's Baddest Man, slated for 2027.

#3888. Sony have cancelled Fairgame$, once again reminding us that chasing live service big bucks basically never works

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

#3887. Xbox is testing a way to use your phone as a controller on smart TVs

Xbox is testing two new ways to play its cloud games, and one of them doesn't require a controller at all.

Announced on Xbox Wire on 4th November, the phone controller preview is rolling out on supported TVs wherever Xbox Cloud Gaming is available. The phone option - which works with both Android and iOS devices - lets you use your phone "as a controller when you don't have one nearby". Connect to your TV via QR code, and the controls open in your phone's browser.

The second preview, called cloud connect, is currently limited to the US and lets the new Xbox Nano controller talk to your cloud session over wi- fi instead of pairing directly with your TV to "help reduce input latency, so gameplay feels more responsive".

To try out the phone controls yourself, switch on Preview Features under Settings > Account in the latest version of the Xbox smart TV app.

Xbox has published a setup guide with full instructions, although you should note that both experiences "are still being tested", so the availability and supported games or devices "may be limited while [Xbox] learns from your feedback".

ICYMI, as of yesterday, anyone in the Xbox Insider Program can try Microsoft's updated Xbox PC app. The company claims it now boots up 60% faster, several pages can launch up to 50 percent faster, and in-app windows can open up to 65 percent faster.

#3885. DOOM: The Dark Ages DLC ‘Revelations’ – ‘Slaughter Mode’ update launches November 16

Publisher Bethesda Softworks and developer id Software will release a free update for DOOM: The Dark Ages paid downloadable content “Revelations” on November 16 that adds the endless combat mode, “Slaughter Mode,” the companies announced.

Push your slaying skills to the limit with Slaughter Mode, a new endless combat challenge available November 16 as a free update for owners of DOOM: The Dark Ages downloadable content “Revelations.”

Tear through relentless, escalating and unpredictable waves of demonic hordes, carving out your personal best scores and unlocking rewards using the Skulls collected from the carnage. With each checkpoint reached, players must ask themselves if they want to cash in their run or risk it all for more slaughter.

No two runs through Slaughter Mode are identical as you fight escalating rounds of random encounters, bosses and arenas, turning up the heat as you proceed further into your run.

Complete rounds to earn Skulls, which unlock rewards such as Slaughter Mode-only Slayer skins, weapon skins for all modes and profile icons. You can also unlock tracks from Andrew Hulshult’s IDKFA soundtrack to play in both Slaughter Mode and the Ripatorium! Take on weekly challenges for more opportunities to earn rewards and show off your slaying prowess.

Survive long enough to reach a Round Checkpoint and you’ll have the chance to Secure your current Skulls against death. Choose Risk It instead to add to your Skull Multiplier, increasing the Skulls you can earn during the run—but there’s a catch. If you’re slain while Risk It is active, all your unsecured Skulls are forfeited!

Death isn’t the end, however: every Round Checkpoint you complete also unlocks another starting point for future runs, letting you resume the carnage in those later encounters sooner.

DOOM: The Dark Ages is available now for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store. It is also available via Game Pass.

Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. #3883. Wardogs Season 3 brings an urban map, Limited Mode, and a 185,000-account ban wave

Wardogs' Season 3 will launch on 12th November, complete with a new urban map, a new Limited Mode, and a ban wave targeting 185,000 accounts.

Developer Bulkhead confirmed the details earlier this week, revealing plans for a full wipe and progression changes that it hopes will "recapture the shared discovery and sense of achievement that defined" the 100-player tactical shooter when it first launched in Early Access.

The new map will focus on close-quarters fighting, and for a "more level playing field", players can dip into Limited Mode, which offers "an alternative way to experience" the game as it restricts weapons, ammunition, armour, and vehicles.

While the full list of restrictions is still being decided, it currently includes FMJ-only ammunition, a Tier 2 armour cap, and a reduced attack vehicle selection.

"The mode is designed to preserve the feel of early-to-mid-game combat and reduce the advantage offered by more powerful equipment," the team said.

Bulkhead also confirmed seasons are getting longer. From now on, they’ll last three months, giving players "more time to work towards their goals before each wipe and the development team more time to prepare future updates". Progression will also be "brought closer to the pace of Season 1", following the studio’s acknowledgement that Season 2 accelerated "the journey too aggressively".

"Season 3 is about giving players a new battlefield to learn together and a progression journey worth spending time on," said Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer. "Longer seasons give everyone more room to reach their own goals, and give us the time to properly develop what comes next."

Alongside Season 3, Bulkhead revealed it has used machine learning to review is "activating further layers of its anti-cheat" after analysing 187 million hours of gameplay with help from machine learning. It says having close to four million unique players since launch gave it enough data to pull that work forward from next year.

"[E]xploiters, real-money traders, and gold-farming networks" have been permanently banned and lost their server-hosting privileges, and a player trust score is planned for 2027.

"Protecting the people who play Wardogs fairly is essential to everything we're building," Brammer added.

Bigger changes to the metagame, including a new progression system, are also due in 2027 as Bulkhead works towards Wardogs 1.0. Full Season 3 patch notes will be out before launch.

Wardogs launched in Steam Early Access on 10th September, and is due on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S in 2028.

Wardogs is one of the breakout successes of the year. In our early access Wardogs review, we said the game's mix of competitive shooters' best bits with something entirely of its own made it "a brilliantly refreshing take on the genre".

We PC gamers are far from the belle of the AI ball.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as Nvidia CEO. That's such an odd sentence to write, as a huge part of my career as a tech journalist has revolved around covering Nvidia, its graphics cards, and its leather-jacketed chief.

As I write this article, I'm already seeing reactions on social media from PC gamers. Some are shocked, some are indifferent, and some appear to be celebrating. In terms of the latter, I'd imagine that's because the ex-Nvidia boss has become one of the most recognisable figures behind the great AI revolution, which, err, isn't popular within our hobby, to say the least.

Not only that, but RAM is ludicrously expensive, with storage not far behind. And graphics cards, Nvidia's gaming bread and butter? The price increases recently have been mind-boggling. All of these things are, in the main, AI server-demand induced, and Nvidia is behind the chips that power most of those servers, making vast amounts of money in the process.

And so on that level, I can understand why some might cheer his departure, equating the company's figurehead with Nvidia's new place in the AI economy as a whole—leaving us gamers in the lurch. But as far as I see it, Jensen Huang leaving the helm of Nvidia is unlikely to be a good thing for PC gaming.

I'll give you an unfortunate percentage: 7.4%. That's roughly how much of Nvidia's total revenue was brought in by gaming in the 2026 fiscal year. The company reported $193.7 billion in data center revenue. Its gaming division? $16 billion. That's despite the fact the company is estimated to hold 90% of the PC graphics card market share.

In terms of business fundamentals, Nvidia would be foolish to put more focus on gaming hardware while the AI cash cow continues to provide. Huang, however, still seemed reluctant to leave PC gaming entirely by the wayside during his tenure.

Those who have watched as many Nvidia GPU announcements as I have will know that walking on stage with a new graphics card, or gaming laptop, lit up Huang's face the most. 3D graphics was where the company began, after all, back when founders Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem sat down at a Denny's in San Jose and put together a business plan. Or so the story goes.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

But now, someone new will be steering the ship. Colette Kress, the company's executive vice president and chief financial officer will serve as interim CEO, while the search begins for Huang's permanent replacement.

Whoever they are, they'll be taking over an absolute titan of tech, the behemoth standing behind the US position in the great AI race, and a company that will need to convince its investors that the AI good times are far from over. How big a factor do you think consumer graphics cards are likely to be in those discussions?

Personally, I reckon they're going to be pretty far down the list of priorities. Because this is big business, money talks, and AI data centers are where most of the cash still lies. I wish that wasn't true, but the figures speak for themselves.

So, if Nvidia pivots even further away from gaming hardware, where might your next graphics card come from? There's always AMD, who's CEO has recently proudly declared it as "a data center-first company." Hmm, I'm not too confident on the focus there, either. Or Intel, which... oh jeez, you too?

I'm not saying consumer gaming hardware, or Nvidia graphics cards, are going to disappear entirely in the face of the AI onslaught. But what I am saying is that, love him or loathe him, Jensen Huang was still an advocate for PC gaming—at least out of sentimentality, if nothing else.

He who became one of the primary movers of the AI market now threatening our hobby, was also an integral part of PC gaming's success. But now, Nvidia is likely to be making some big changes, sans Huang—and I find it hard to believe that many of them will be in our favour.

#3881. Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell says. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio."

Just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

As for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.)

None of this is intended to be a knock on Dawn of War 4. From what I've played it's a very good Warhammer 40K RTS, if it perhaps sticks a little closely to the model laid down by Relic's original. What do I know, though, talking about their own games, Dowdeswell tells me that while "one of the messages to the studio is we can't just make [the same] things that we made 20 years ago and hope it goes well", re-releasing the 20-year-old Dawn of War sold very well for Relic and netted the team some very positive reviews on Steam. "There's a bit of a paradox there," he adds"

Anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell says. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it."

Relic and new owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Company of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent update is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell says foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly."

I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had plans to release new games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a big part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Company of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a new game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future."

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer."

#3880. Assassin's Creed is reportedly going to ancient Rome, while a mobile spin-off heads to Jerusalem

Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games, and one of them is set in ancient Rome.

That's according to YouTuber Xj0nathan, who says the Rome game is codenamed Mars. He claims two sources with access to Ubisoft's backend systems backed up the information, and that the setting will likely be linked to the upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series.

The second game, codenamed Pocket, is said to be a mobile title set in Jerusalem. Xj0nathan claims it'll play a bit like Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s Mastery Challenge, and look similar to the most recent Prince of Persia. The hero's mentor is apparently a character called Myriam.

Insider Gaming says it's heard the codenames too, but couldn't confirm them well enough to report them independently. It puts some of that down to the turbulence the franchise has gone through since former Assassin's Creed boss Marc-Alexis Côté left Ubisoft.

Last month, the outlet's sources also claimed Assassin's Creed Hexe, the next mainline game, had been delayed internally by another year, likely to 2028. Other reports claim we'll see it next year.

If Mars does move into full production, don't hold your breath - Insider Gaming doesn't expect us to hear anything about it until 2029 or 2030.

Assassin's Creed has visited Rome before, in 2010’s Brotherhood, but that was the Renaissance version of the city.

The leak comes less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

The finale of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy dares to expand even further from its world to character customization

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you thought Final Fantasy 7 Revelation was going to rein things in after the maximalist scale of Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, then think again. This is, after all, the finale of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy, so it's got to go out with a bang. Square Enix has also, so far, designed each instalment to be its own standalone RPG with a raft of new gameplay features rather than just a mere iteration of the next episode of the story.

While Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is already confirmed to be the largest entry to date – literally so with a file size estimated to be up to 200GB – there's plenty of new features that make this stand out from the already colossal achievements of its predecessors. This may still be a single-player story-driven party-based action RPG set over a planet-sized open world, but the developers have cooked up a lot more that demonstrates why it wasn't just called Final Fantasy 7 Remake Part 3.

There's potentially still more that Square Enix will reveal as the finale's April 8 launch date approaches, but from our hands-on time and official announcements made so far, these are the eight new features coming to Final Fantasy 7 Revelation that we feel is going to make this the most definitive of all the remake releases to date.

With the remake trilogy drawing to a close early 2027, we get ready for the epic conclusion with our Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Big Preview across hands-on impressions, dev access, and deep dives into the whole adventure so far.

Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth had already given us the impossible with an open world that really does encompass a world, and while Final Fantasy 7 Revelation adds to that with still several more locations, including Mideel and Wutai, its planetary scale has been magnified with verticality. You're not just fast-traveling to locations, but you have Cid's airship, the Highwind, which you can use to fly over any location and then jump out and parachute down seamlessly in real-time.

It's already a huge change from the original game where you could only access part of the overworld if you had enough space to land the Highwind. Instead of just warping to a set checkpoint, it also means if there's a nearby side quest marker, you can glide that way directly, or there might be another secret at a higher elevation you hadn't noticed before that's worth trying to land at to investigate. It's certainly a way to make revisiting places feel fresh again in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation.

While Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth had a new chocobo for each region, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation reunites you with yellow-feathered chocobo Piko from the Grasslands, this time as your sole mount. That might sound like something this instalment is reining in, but what it actually means is Piko will feel like a permanent addition to the party. Not just a mount for getting you from A to B, they'll actually level up and can even fight alongside you in battle.

Old-school fans may lament that there won't be chocobo-breeding like the original game, but I think having Piko grow and unlock new abilities, both in terms of traversal and combat, during your journey makes for a more meaningful companion than any other gaming mount. It's not like The Witcher 3's Roach was ever useful in a fight.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

Although Cid Highwind and Vincent Valentine were introduced in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, they become fully playable party members in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. While it will be exciting getting to grips with Cid's dragoon-style fighting style or Vincent's Galian beast transformation, you'll also be able to select them or any of the other party members as the playable character during exploration.

Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth did also try to mix things up occasionally in dungeons where the party would get split up or put you in control of a certain character in story-specific missions. Nonetheless, this small but meaningful change means you can spend more time controlling your favorite character while out in the wider world. It also makes sense given the story will cover the section when central protagonist Cloud will be out of action. And if you play as Vincent, it might be the closest we'll get to a Dirge of Cerberus remaster – it could still happen, right?

Arguably the most significant new feature in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is the FITS (Function-Integrated Tactical Suitwear) system, which may also sound rather similar to Dresspheres for any Final Fantasy 10-2 fans. Essentially, you can give each party member new threads or armor that also give them new classes that recall classic Final Fantasy jobs, such as Knight, Black Mage, or Summoner.

There's real style to this too as each outfit is tailored to each character rather than wearing the same job uniform. The abilities that come with each outfit are also actually additions rather than changing your class entirely, so if Tifa is dressed as a white mage, rest assured you can still kick ass with her divekick as before. That also means, if you're not looking to think too deeply about builds and just like the outfits as a cosmetic, then that's totally viable too.

The Black Materia is going to be a crucial plot point in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, as it's what allows Sephiroth to summon Meteor, and its ominous presence in the sky is going to be inescapable as you play through the game. Its activation will however also cause significant change to the world, notably the emergence of Weapons roaming the world.

Perhaps more significant is how the effects of Black Materia may alter the world's terrain. We can only speculate at this point what that can mean, but taking the addition of the Highwind and Piko into account as new ways of traversal, don't be surprised if the Grasslands suddenly has new structures or a rupture in the ground that require more verticality in traversal to explore. Call it the Tears of the Kingdom effect, but it should also mean you aren't just going back to explore the exact same regions as you left them in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth.

Equipping Materia to use spells or gain buffs remains a key aspect of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, though being treated as its own standalone game, I won't be surprised if that means having to upgrade them and find new Materia again, even if you might start with a default number of them as with Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth.

But, one area this finale plans to go further is how many Materia you can potentially link together. While we have already had gear that could link two Materia together, there may also be armor that can link three Materia together. That could mean being able to Magnify Materia to two separate spells so that they both reap the benefits, or potentially other uses that I'm still racking my brain over.

Synergy was a cool feature introduced in Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth where you can have two party members team up together in battle. These ranged from real-time Synergy Skills like Aerith calling another party member to be her bodyguard or Tifa getting someone to launch her towards an enemy, to Synergy Abilities as show-stopping as Limit Breaks. How do you top that? Triple Synergy!

Given the three-person party size that was also true of the original game, it seems such a logical conclusion to have them all unite in one killer combo. That said, given the complexity of coordinating three characters simultaneously, I suspect this may just be limited to an ultimate ability that may only be available in specific situations, but expect them to leave a lasting impression.

Players looking for a proper challenge in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation don't need to finish the game to unlock a hard mode. Given how long this finale is going to be, that's already a tall order. But it also doesn't mean it's going to be hard mode available from the start but with that mode's item restrictions or enemies with double the health as with past games.

What it actually means in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is that because of the huge amount of side quests available and freedom to explore from very early on, there is absolutely nothing stopping you from taking on the toughest side quests and bosses even if you've vastly underleveled, while there are of course also the Weapons roaming the land, just tempting you to go pick a fight, whether or not you're ready.

Our best Final Fantasy games ranking is a revelation when it comes to finding something new to play to plug the gap while you wait for more, while our best RPGs, best JRPGs, and best ARPGs lists have even more!

#3877. Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Currently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

My computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw quickly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is launched over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

The worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

Casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

#3876. Sony delays PlayStation's Pulse Elevate speakers indefinitely, less than a week before launch

Sony has delayed its Pulse Elevate wireless speakers indefinitely, less than a week before they were due to launch.

The news came in a 6th November update to Sony’s original announcement on the PlayStation Blog, first spotted by IGN. Quality testing has turned up a "production issue", Sony said, and there's no new release date yet.

"As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production issue with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch," the statement reads. "The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologise for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon."

The speakers were set to go on sale worldwide on 12th November, and pre-orders opened in September. It's unclear what, exactly, happens to those orders, but we'll update as and when we find out more.

Sony revealed Pulse Elevate in September 2025 as its first wireless speakers for desktop gaming. They sit alongside the Pulse Elite headset and Pulse Explore earbuds, and cost £199.99 ($219.99).

They connect to PS5, PC, Mac, and PlayStation Portal via PlayStation Link, and can pair with a phone over Bluetooth at the same time. There's also a microphone in the right speaker with what Sony calls "AI-enhanced noise rejection".

Midnight Black was due to be available everywhere, while the White version was limited to a handful of countries, including the UK.

Alongside the Pulse Elevate speakers, Sony revealed a range of hardware in September 2025, including a 27-inch gaming monitor that's coming only to the US and Japan.

Tae Kim, author of The Nvidia Way, thinks there are some promising alternatives to Huang.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great.November 11, 2026

We thought it might be coming, and it's here: Jensen Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia, as he has resigned following an admitted affair, and an additional alleged one.

It wasn't unexpected, and both before and after the announcement there has been a lot of talk about how it would be a bad decision and could spell very bad news for Nvidia. And, well, there's certainly some truth in that given we saw company share prices drop after reports of Huang's alleged second affair came to light.

After perusing X for a while today, the general sentiment seems to be that Huang was so incredibly central to Nvidia that the company couldn't possibly do well without him. Or at the very least, nowhere near as well as it would with Jensen sticking at the helm. Ditto the AI market in general.

But not everyone agrees. In fact, one of the most credible voices on Nvidia reckons there are "strong" and "excellent" candidates for a replacement. Tae Kim wrote the most well-known, authoritative book on the company—The Nvidia Way—and yesterday they explained:

"Many people have cited my book as saying Nvidia would be completely lost without Jensen Huang. My views have evolved in the several years since I wrote those passages. I now believe there is a strong internal candidate with the technical expertise, experience, customer relationships and respect of employees needed to lead Nvidia effectively into its next chapter."

"There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great."

They're certainly optimistic comments, but your guess is as good as mine as to who they might be referring to—presumably someone on the list of potential replacement CEO candidates I put together earlier.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

We now know that the actual interim CEO is Colette Kress—exactly who we predicted it would be. I'm not sure whether that's who Kim had in mind, given they decided, for some strange reason, to not mention who they were thinking of by name. But if not, there's still room for the next proper CEO to be one of those he has in mind.

This being said, Jensen Huang's status, drive, and deep familiarity with the company and the market are undoubtedly unparalleled. I think you'd find it difficult to pin down anyone who could reasonably disagree with that. In which case, while Nvidia might not be "completely lost", it's hard to say it will be as oriented as it would be with Huang still at the helm.

3. Best mid-range: Nvidia RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB

Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. He swiftly realised the local PC repair store had ripped him off with his build and vowed never to let another soul build his rig again. With this vow, Jacob the hardware junkie was born. Since then, Jacob's led a double-life as part-hardware geek, part-philosophy nerd, first working as a Hardware Writer for PCGamesN in 2020, then working towards a PhD in Philosophy for a few years while freelancing on the side for sites such as TechRadar, Pocket-lint, and yours truly, PC Gamer. Eventually, he gave up the ruthless mercenary life to join the world's #1 PC Gaming site full-time. It's definitely not an ego thing, he assures us.

#3874. Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World details early adventure

Publisher and developer Square Enix, and developer TOSE have released new information and screenshots for Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World introducing protagonists Bianca and Nera‘s early adventure, Witherwood Castle, and the surrounding Witherwood region.

■ Explore a Strange World with a Team of Your Favorite Monsters!

Thursday, December 3, 2026, marks the simultaneous worldwide release date of Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World. Our protagonists on this adventure are none other than Bianca and Nera from Dragon Quest V: Hand of the Heavenly Bride. A mysterious fairy transports the girls to Witherwood, a kingdom in an unfamiliar world, where they hope to obtain some Leaves of Life that they believe will cure their sick fathers. However, Witherwood is beset by dark forces that have drained the land of its living energy, all but eradicating the Leaves of Life from existence. To ensure the Leaves of Life will grow once more, Bianca and Nera must become monster wranglers—plucky types with the power to befriend monsters—and lead their team of loyal allies on an adventure across this strange new world.

—Take your favorite monsters along with you as you explore all corners of the world. What new adventures await you beyond the curve of the horizon?

—You can now scout monsters on the fly as you explore, as well as in battle. It’s never been easier to befriend all the monsters you want!

—The Synthesis feature lets you combine two monsters to create a new one. You’ll have to synthesize many, many monsters on your quest to build a powerful party.

—It’s your job to rid the world of the evil forces that drain the land of its life energy.

■ The Early Adventure: Becoming a Monster Wrangler

Soon after arriving in Witherwood to look for the Leaves of Life, Bianca and Nera are given the power to befriend monsters and set out on their quest as fledgeling monster wranglers. Once you’ve decided which character you want to control and have your starting monster, it’s time for you to go off and befriend a few more!

—You can choose to begin the adventure as either Bianca or Nera. Each protagonist will find it easier to befriend monsters from different families, and their Wrangler’s Sprit ability provides different beneficial effects when it activates during battle. So, examine their differences and pick your favorite!

—After you answer Fluffy’s questions, he’ll present you with your first monster. The monster you get depends on your responses, but there’s no need to overthink things!

—When you enter battle, the monsters you’ve befriended will fight under your command. Give them specific orders or set their general tactics and march your way to victory!

—Use a Show of Force in battle to attempt to befriend an enemy monster. If you succeed, the monster will join your team. On rare occasions, a monster may even ask to join you of its own accord after a battle ends!

■ The Early Adventure: Witherwood Castle, Your Base of Operations

Witherwood Castle will soon become something of a home base for Bianca and Nera as their adventure ramps up. Conveniently, the castle town is home to many amenities that will serve the girls well on their quest.

The kingdom’s ruler, King Withers, holds court in his throne hall, from where he provides the girls with invaluable advice. See what he has to say if you find yourself at a loss for where to go next.

The paddock is where your monsters hang out when not in your party. From here, you can also access the monster depot when you want to make changes to your team line-up.

The item shop sells a range of wares, including meat, which monsters absolutely love! The stock changes as you progress through the story, so check back regularly to see what’s new.

As the story unfolds, you’ll start to see changes in Witherwood Castle and the adjoining town. For starters, a monster called Tony will appear and challenge you to complete scouting trials for a reward, and townsfolk will offer their monsters to you for synthesis in the form of matchmaking opportunities. Also, the accessories you can equip to your monsters can be upgraded at a workshop that will open after a while. Witherwood has plenty on offer to help our young wranglers strengthen their team in preparation for the next step of their adventure!

This odd monster will give you clues describing a very specific monster he wants you to show him. The trials get more difficult with each one you complete, but the rewards get better to match.

Some townsfolk will offer you their monsters to use for synthesis. You can contribute any monster you like, but if you can provide the one the townsperson mentions, you’ll be able to perform a special synthesis!

With the right crafting materials and enough gold, you can upgrade your accessories twice at most. You’ll find these materials when you’re out exploring, but monsters sometimes drop them after battle as well.

■ The Early Adventure: Exploring the Witherwood Region

Once all the preparations are complete, it’s time to start exploring the game’s first main area: Witherwood! The region is divided into several sub-areas, each with its own distinct vibe and unique changes that occur as the day shifts to night. With Roots of Creation and Lifebuds to locate, as well as super-strong monsters and dungeons to discover, every area is worth exploring to its fullest.

Each area is home to monsters that may disappear or behave differently as day becomes night. For example, the teenie sanguini is strictly nocturnal, meaning you’ll find a different monster if you return to the same place during the daytime.

What to Do With the Withered Roots of Creation and Lifebuds?

—Give a Root of Creation a sprinkle with the Waterwing Can to revive it. Doing so will add it to the Zoom list for fast travel and create a one-stop-shop for healing monsters, adjusting your party, synthesizing, and changing the time.

—Helping the Lifebuds to bloom will provide your party with permanent passive boosts, such as increased experience points, that will really benefit you. If you see a Lifebud, be sure to give it a drink!

The monsters you see stomping about with a red aura around them are incredibly powerful. You can try fighting them at the start of the game if you really want, but it’s advised to wait until you have a stronger team.

While dungeons are home to hordes of monsters, they also contain valuable treasures, like mini medals that you can exchange for superb prizes at the Mini Medal Swap Swap in Witherwood.

In the depths of a dungeon, a ferocious monster often lies in wait. But before you jump into battle, it’s a good idea to head to a nearby Root of Creation to heal up and prepare your party.

■ The Early Adventure: Strengthen Your Team and Head to the Next Region

Before they can start synthesizing, Bianca and Nera must team up to take down a massive monster in a Joint Battle, as well as emerge victorious at the Battle Arena. But you can’t just synthesize with any old riffraff—you’ll need two monsters at Level 10 or above in order to synthesize a new one. With enough battles under your belt and a few strong monsters synthesized, you’ll be ready to explore the next region: Pays de l’Oseille!

Team Up to Beat the Massive Monster Enorman

—If you’re controlling Bianca for the Joint Battle, she’ll command your main party, with Nera in charge of your reserves—and vice versa if you’re using Nera.

—When a massive monster becomes enraged, each of its attacks will deal heavy damage, but it’ll be more susceptible to damage itself. Keep calm and use the opportunity to attack!

If you find the Battle Arena to be tough going, try leveling up your party and including some monsters in your team that can use spells or healing abilities.

With Both Trials Done, Go to the Starry Shine in the Castle to Start Synthesizing

—If you have two monsters at Level 10 or higher, you can combine them to synthesize a new one. You can even synthesize monsters from any Root of Creation you find out in the wider world.

—Child monsters born through synthesis can inherit the Talents of their parents. Some monsters can only be made through synthesis, so try to explore as many combinations as you can.

A number of regions beyond Witherwood are waiting to be explored. Hunting for treasure in a sunken shipwreck, adventuring among giant fruits and veggies, and many more adventures await you!

Bianca and Nera’s search for the Leaves of Life is only just beginning!

Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is due out for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, Switch, and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store on December 3. A demo is available now.

#3873. Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back

"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together."

Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.

Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected.

Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.

"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you."

Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.

The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month. Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible".

It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week.

In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review, we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".
